judges.note: Two commits bundle distinct concerns. 72f79d7 (T7+T8) mixes the 417-line tests/test_acceptance.py, a production fix (server.py request_queue_size=128), a store.py schema/user_version reorder, a __main__.py docstring and unconditional client import, and a conftest Proc stderr change. Its own subject lists three things: 'acceptance tests, listen backlog and polish'. 37931be (T5+T6) joins the serve/shutdown lifecycle (__main__.py, test_serve.py) with a separate client module (client.py, test_client.py); its subject uses 'and'. f13204f (T3+T4) is defensible: server.py holds both pipeline and handlers, and the body says so. bf81a08 and 19fa925 are one concern each. The plan, plan-review, spec, phase-tracking and impl-review commits are each coherent. I counted the tracking files inside the functional commits as fine, per the Q5 precedent.

Phase 4 commit 72f79d7 (Tasks: T7, T8) mixes unrelated concerns. It adds tests/test_acceptance.py (417 lines). It also changes server.py (request_queue_size=128), store.py (moves PRAGMA user_version after the schema statements) and __main__.py (docstring and unconditional client import), plus a conftest Proc stderr-to-file change. Phase 3 commit 37931be (T5, T6) bundles the serve command (__main__.py, test_serve.py) with a separate client CLI (client.py, test_client.py), and its subject says 'serve ... and client CLI'. Phase 2 commit f13204f (T3+T4) is defensible, since server.py holds both and the message says so, and the tracking files in the chore and notes commits are fine under the Q5/D97 precedent. 72f79d7 and 37931be still fall short of the protocol's 'split into multiple small logically-grouped commits, one concern per commit' (execution-protocol.md:44, step 16). Phases 2-4 each got a single functional commit, so about 2 of the 5 functional commits are multi-concern. Commits 8f57795, 4f48861, ff20572, 19fa925, bf81a08, the chore(phase-N) commits and 5ee75ce are each one concern.

Two functional commits mix distinct concerns. 37931be (feat(lifecycle): serve command ... 'and client CLI', Tasks: T5, T6) bundles the serve/shutdown lifecycle in __main__.py with a separate client.py module and its own test_client.py and test_serve.py. 72f79d7 (Tasks: T7, T8) bundles the new 417-line acceptance tests with three unrelated production edits: the server.py request_queue_size backlog fix, a store.py PRAGMA user_version reorder, and an __main__.py optional-import removal plus docstring. Execution-protocol step 16 allows several tasks on one commit only 'when their changes form one concern'. f13204f (T3+T4, both in server.py, rationale stated in the body) is defensible, and the phase/tracking chore commits and plan/spec/impl-review docs commits are each one concern (Q5 precedent).

No commit crosses a phase boundary. 8f57795 is spec only. 4f48861 is plan only. ff20572 is plan-review only. bf81a08 and 19fa925 hold Phase 1 tasks T1-T2. f13204f holds Phase 2 T3-T4. 37931be holds Phase 3 T5-T6. 72f79d7 holds Phase 4 T7-T8. 5ee75ce is impl-review docs only. The chore(phase-N) commits (93ff08d, fbe2fe4, 63d1306, 88e14a4) touch only handoff, kanban and notes for their own phase. Weakness: Phases 2-4 each got one functional commit instead of the finer split the protocol asks for (execution-protocol.md:44, 168), and 88e14a4 was committed 5s before the 72f79d7 code it describes. This is a grouping-granularity problem, not a phase straddle.

No commit straddles a geeky phase. The spec (8f57795), plan (4f48861) and plan-review (ff20572) are separate commits. Implementation commits map to P1: bf81a08 and 19fa925, P2: f13204f, P3: 37931be, P4: 72f79d7. The kanban, handoff and notes updates are separate chore(phase-N) commits (93ff08d, fbe2fe4, 63d1306, 88e14a4), and the impl-review verdict is separate (5ee75ce). A stricter reading of 'one concern per commit' would carry the 72f79d7 and 37931be failures into dp13.

No commit crosses a geeky phase boundary. Spec, plan, plan-review, P1-P4 and impl-review each land in their own commits (8f57795, 4f48861, ff20572, bf81a08/19fa925, 5ee75ce). But dp13 also requires one concern per commit per phase. P2, P3 and P4 each got a single functional commit, so the 'multiple small logically-grouped commits' split was not applied there. The orchestrator's own chore(phase-4) commit 88e14a4 was also made before the feat commit 72f79d7. Verdict is borderline: the phase-straddle half passes, the per-commit concern half fails. Confidence medium.

All 12 commit SHAs match `git log`. The 73-character subject rejection, which left 88e14a4 before 72f79d7, is real and disclosed. Minor omissions only: the T4 coder edited a T3 test and left stray logs, and the kanban release-gate checklist is still unchecked, but none of this is misstated.

Serializing was consistent with the plan: implementation-plan.md:16 says 'Sequential order T1..T8 (each depends on its predecessor)', and every tasks/Tx.md lists its predecessor as its Dependency. The orchestrator stated the reasons in transcript text: :224 says the parallelization suggestions stay optional and the linear order stays binding. :322 says 'T4 builds on T3's server.py'. :388 says 'T6 needs T5's subprocess fixture'. :433 says 'T8 depends on T7'. Weakness: the protocol (step 5) says to record the justification in per-task notes, and grep of tasks/*.notes.md and handoff.md finds no parallel/serial rationale. T1->T2 and T4->T5 have no specific stated reason beyond the declared chain, even though the plan-review at :220 called the chain over-serialized. Passing because serializing is the safe direction and the decision was explicit.

Serialization was correct but was only partly stated. The transcript gives dependency reasons for T3->T4 (session.jsonl:322 'T4 builds on T3's server.py'), T5->T6 (:388) and T7->T8 (:433). T1->T2 has no stated reason (:266, :279). Protocol step 10 and the Parallelization rules require a 'Parallelization decision and justification' in each tasks/Tx-*.notes.md. No notes file, handoff.md or kanban.md contains any parallel/serial/sequential record (git grep empty; T2/T4 notes are one-liners). Only implementation-plan.md:16 says 'Sequential order'. Lean fail on the literal rule; a lenient reading that accepts the in-transcript reasons plus the plan would pass.

The serialization is only partly explained. The orchestrator did state reasons for some pairs: 'T4 builds on T3's server.py' (session.jsonl:322), 'T6 needs T5's subprocess fixture' (:388), 'T8 depends on T7' (:433). It also recorded in review-plan.md:24 that the optional speedups were declined ('T3/T4 share server.py; run is single-session sequential... linear order remains binding'), and the :224 text gives the same decision. But no per-task notes file or handoff.md records the parallelization decision, which execution-protocol.md:126 and :209 require. For T1 to T2, the architect had called the dependency 'weak' and the pair 'true parallel'; the only reason given for waiting was reviewer timing ('Phase 1 can't be reviewed until it finishes', :279). The protocol checklist was never applied explicitly, so I judge the justification insufficient.
